pages.text: $(italic)$(#6b5a45)You edit $(#8a5a2b)exploration_regions$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) in a datapack and $(#8a5a2b)/reload$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) picks it up at once. Before you start, look at the files the server writes for itself — whatever you mean to override is probably already in there.$()$(br2)When a player opens or breaks a naturally generated chest out in the world, the town is paid a sum of experience and elements. That payout is not stored on the chest; it is worked out from the $(bold)loot table$(): the mod reads the whole table's weights, works out the expected yield of one opening, then prices every item through the element mappings and adds it up.
Region configs load through the ordinary datapack path, $(#8a5a2b)data/<namespace>/exploration_regions/<id>.json$().
pages.title: Where the Files Go

pages.text: There is a second tier the server writes for itself, under $(#8a5a2b)<world>/wandscape/generated_regions/$(): every time the server starts, the mod walks all loot tables, prices the chest tables that no region declares, and writes the result as a file in the same format.$(br2)Between the two tiers the $(bold)declared one wins$() — as soon as a region you wrote matches, the generated file of the same name steps aside on its own, and you never have to delete it.
pages.title: The Self-Written Tier

pages.text: The top level holds just two keys. $(#8a5a2b)name$() is the display name, shown in the HUD notice when a player opens a chest; $(#8a5a2b)loot_table_patterns$() is a list of regexes matched against the loot table's full id, such as $(#8a5a2b)minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon$().
pages.title: Which Chests It Claims

pages.text: Matching is won $(bold)on specificity$(): of every region that matches, the one whose patterns carry the most literal characters wins, ties broken by region id. You can therefore write one $(#8a5a2b).*$() region to catch everything, and it will only take effect where no more specific region fits — the result does not depend on the order files load in.$(br2)You do not need anchors: a pattern is accepted on a full match or on a substring match.
pages.title: How a Match Is Chosen

pages.text: The $(#8a5a2b)reward$() block says where the value comes from. $(#8a5a2b)mode$() picks the source of the element value vector:$(br2)$(li)$(#8a5a2b)derived$() (the default) reads the loot table's weights and works out the expectation, with nothing written down.$(li)$(#8a5a2b)fixed$() uses only the numbers in $(#8a5a2b)value$() and never touches the loot table.$(li)$(#8a5a2b)additive$() adds $(#8a5a2b)value$() on top of the sampled expectation.
pages.title: What It Pays

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)value$() maps an element to an amount, keyed by one of the seven elements. $(bold)If you write a $(#8a5a2b)value$()$(bold) without moving $(#8a5a2b)mode$()$(bold) to $(#8a5a2b)fixed$()$(bold) or $(#8a5a2b)additive$()$(bold), the value is logged as a warning and ignored$() — "written but doing nothing" is the expensive kind of quiet, so this one gets loud.
pages.title: The value Field

pages.text: $(bold)Key  Effect$()$(li)exp_ratio — experience = the vector's total ÷ this ratio, default 15.0, and never below a floor of 15$(li)danger_multiplier — a danger factor that scales experience only, never elements, default 1.0$(li)variance — how far the roll spreads, default 0.25 for plus or minus 25%$(li)loot_share — the fraction of the element total that keeps the loot table's proportions; the rest is spread over the seven elements, default 0.5
pages.title: The Four Parameters

pages.text: The danger factor multiplies experience alone, so the element total never moves — a dangerous region is "expensive experience, ordinary elements".

Pricing through the element mappings measures what it costs to build the things in the table. That is an honest reflection of a chest's worth, but it sits below how rewarding finding one should feel, so $(bold)the estimated vector is doubled before it enters the formulas above$().$(br2)A number you wrote into $(#8a5a2b)value$() is used exactly as written — whoever writes a number means that number.
pages.title: How the Estimate Is Priced

pages.text: When no item in the loot table has an element mapping — another mod's chests are the usual case — the vector is empty and the payout is zero: no experience, no elements, no particles, no HUD notice, just one line in the log.$(br2)That is deliberate: a small consolation payout only makes "no data" look like "a cheap chest" and hides the real problem.
pages.title: Nothing Priced, Nothing Paid

pages.text: The payout settles when a player right-clicks a naturally generated container or breaks it, and a given position only ever counts once. What it keys off is the container being $(bold)still unopened, with a loot table still attached$() — vanilla clears the table the first time a chest is opened, and a chest a player placed never had one, so there is nothing to farm.
pages.title: When It Settles

pages.text: A double chest counts once for the whole chest, and container entities such as chest minecarts work the same way.

The Settings Center's Town tab carries two dials, an exploration chest experience multiplier and an element multiplier, each settable from 0 to 10 times. They multiply at the very last step, so they cover both the estimate and a hand-written $(#8a5a2b)value$() alike — that is an administrator's global switch, not an region setting, and it is not the way to tune one region.
pages.title: Global Multipliers
